title: the keyed search's index as a bit mask, 0x141b330c0
notes: Read from the body: the four arguments are forwarded unchanged to 0x141b331f0, then `mov ecx,eax; xor edx,edx; mov eax,1; shl rax,cl; cmp ecx,-1; cmove rax,rdx` - so the result is 0 for -1 and 1 << (index & 63) otherwise.
The shift masks `cl` to six bits, which only shows on a table with more than 64 records: case 0 is 70 records with the match at index 64, so the result is 1 (1 << 0), not 1 << 64.
Composition unit: the callee 0x141b331f0 is fn/KeyTableFind, verified separately, and this unit proves the wrapper's own two instructions.

knownEquivalentMutants.rationale: Widening `& 63` to a wider mask cannot change the result on x86-64: `1u64 << n` lowers to `shl rax, cl`, and the instruction masks the count to six bits itself, so the explicit mask is redundant at machine level. Equivalent for this target (and NOT in the abstract - a shift by 64 is undefined in Rust), which is exactly why the client's `cl` use and this line agree.
